contribution: A sequential psychiatry benchmark shows most LLMs diagnose despite insufficient evidence, with under-abstention above 60% for most models even when prompted that abstaining is allowed.

title: Removable Defects: The Economics and Limits of Deliberate Deficiency

title: Verification-Gated Agentic Mission-State Governance for Intelligent Industrial Multi-Robot Systems
authors: Guoqin Tang; Qingxuan Jia; Yichen Tan; Zeyuan Huang; Ning Ji; Gang Chen

title: Certified Speculative Execution for Untrusted AI Agents

title: Budgeted Act-or-Defer Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation with Local Reliability Bounds
authors: M. Wang; Haochen Xie; Guang-Hui Wang; Devin Zhang; Jae Oh Woo
contribution: Turns multi-agent debate into a budgeted act-or-defer rule with a proved conditional bound on wrong actions, acting autonomously on 9 to 84 percent of questions while keeping wrong actions near 2 to 9 percent.

title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?
authors: Han Luo; Bingbing Wen; Lucy Lu Wang

title: Capability Minimization as a Safety Primitive: Risk-Aware Causal Gating for Least-Privilege LLM Agents
authors: Laxmipriya Ganesh Iyer; Rahul Suresh Babu

title: Designing for Doubt: The Case for Informed Abstention in Autonomous Agents
authors: Victor Ojewale; Suresh Venkatasubramanian
contribution: Position paper with a preliminary study: a pre-execution checkpoint wrapper that vetoes under-specified or unauthorised tool calls raises agent safety rate to 87.5-90.8% across seven model families.

title: BOKBO (Best of K Bad Options): Calibrated Abstention for VLA Policies
authors: Anya Singh; Cabrel Happi; Jai Relan; Varun Nair; Vidyut Baradwaj

authors: Laerdon Kim; Vivian Nguyen; Cristian Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil

title: Retrying vs Resampling in AI Control

title: Density-Ratio Losses for Post-Hoc Learning to Defer
authors: Alexander Soen; Ragnar Thobaben; Joakim Jaldén; Richard Nock

authors: Dang Hoang Duy; Yannis Montreuil; Maxime Meyer; Axel Carlier; Lai Xing Ng; Wei Tsang Ooi

contribution: A router that separates reducible from irreducible uncertainty to choose between answering, deferring to a stronger oracle and abstaining, with a proved excess-cost bound under higher-order calibration.

title: Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings
authors: Corinna Cortes; Anqi Mao; Mehryar Mohri; Yutao Zhong
contribution: A margin-based surrogate for two-stage learning to defer when some experts are rarely the best choice, with generalisation and consistency bounds and gains over the standard two-stage loss.

authors: Qi Tian; Haoliang Sun; Yunshan Wang; Ying-Huan Shi; Yi-Long Yin

title: Who Should Predict? Exact Algorithms For Learning to Defer to Humans
authors: Mozannar, Hussein; Lang, Hunter; Wei, Dennis; Sattigeri, Prasanna; Das, Subhro; Sontag, David

title: Cost-Sensitive Learning to Defer to Multiple Experts with Workload Constraints
authors: Alves, Jean V.; Leitão, Diogo; Jesus, Sérgio; Sampaio, Marco O.P.; Liébana, Javier; Saleiro, Pedro; Figueiredo, Mário A. T.; Bizarro, Pedro

title: A Two-Stage Learning-to-Defer Approach for Multi-Task Learning
authors: Montreuil, Yannis; Yeo, Shu Heng; Carlier, Axel; Ng, Lai Xing; Ooi, Wei Tsang

authors: Mao, Anqi; Mohri, Mehryar; Zhong, Yutao

title: A Unifying Post-Processing Framework for Multi-Objective Learn-to-Defer Problems
authors: Charusaie, Mohammad-Amin; Samadi, Samira

title: Optimizing Delegation Between Human and AI Collaborative Agents
authors: Fuchs, Andrew; Passarella, Andrea; Conti, Marco

contribution: Models human-AI delegation as a manager MDP whose actions are choices of which agent acts next, learned from team outcomes alone, and shows in gridworlds that it beats random delegation.

authors: Shah, Vrund; Chaudhari, Tejas; Manwani, Naresh

authors: Narasimhan, Harikrishna; Menon, Aditya Krishna; Jitkrittum, Wittawat; Kumar, Sanjiv

authors: Strong, Joshua; Men, Qianhui; Noble, J. Alison

authors: Gangrade, Aditya; Kag, Anil; Cutkosky, Ashok; Saligrama, Venkatesh
